details: PLAUSIBLE (not measured either way). The design rests its recommendation of links on Claude Code's docs saying symlinks are followed when a
plugin is cached, and states it was "not tested here; the build checks it". The build did not. On this machine sessions read ~/relay/plugins
directly (project memory), so today's sessions are not at risk; the owner's development is moving to Linux VMs, where relay would be installed
through the cache. No existing cache entry holds a symlink to learn from (find ~/.claude/plugins/cache -type l: none).
Size: 15 agent minutes (one scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR install and a find; a test only if it is cheap to keep).
evidence: builder report lib-modules-are-committed-in-three-copie.md: "Pass case 4 (claude plugin install cache) NOT tested."
failing_case: The brief: "Follow its build steps and pass cases, including pass case 4 (how Claude Code's install cache copies a symlink)". The design, pass case 4:
"A plugin installed with `claude plugin install` into a scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR has real files, not links, under its cached lib/ and its hooks
import (if it fails, stop and report: C then needs B's copy for the cache only)". The builder's report: "Pass case 4 (claude plugin install cache)
NOT tested." Now: unknown whether a cached relay plugin holds relay_queue.py as a file or as a dangling link ../../../lib/relay_queue.py; if
the latter, every hook of an installed plugin fails its import and, as a PreToolUse hook exiting 1 is non-blocking, the main-checkout guard and
the routing guard turn off silently. Should: measured once, with the result recorded.
fix_hint: Run the design's pass case 4 in a scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and record the outcome in the report (and in the queue item's notes); stop and report if links survive into the cache.
pass_cases: 1. claude plugin install relay@<local marketplace> with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<scratch>: find <scratch>/plugins/cache -path '*/lib/relay_*.py' -type l prints nothing; each lib/relay_*.py there is a regular file equal to lib/<name>.
2. In that cache folder, each plugins hook (hooks/*.py) run with {} on stdin from the cache folder exits as it does from the repo (no ImportError).
3. If 1 fails: the outcome is reported to the owner before the merge (design: C then needs B's copy for the cache only), not merged silently.

4. Sessions that read the repo folder (today's setup) keep working: hooks from plugins/

/hooks run with {} and import (already green in the gate's hook tests).
reason: Fixer measured a scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR install (real files, hooks import); not reproduced by me, no test possible.
findings.summary: pass case 4 (a plugin installed through Claude Code's cache gets real files and its hooks import) was never run; the design made it a stop condition

details: CONFIRMED by a scratch reproduction calling relay_bench.lib_adoption_conflicts. The comparison is candidate file vs the link's current
target, so "differs" means "candidate edited it OR lib/ moved on since the candidate was made"; the message asserts the first. Candidates
live for a bench run (hours), and lib/ changes many times a day, so the second is the usual case for a --copy candidate. The refusal itself is
safe (nothing is written); the advice is wrong, and an agent following it ports a reverse diff into lib/. Principle 10: a refusal names the
right next step. Before this change the same candidate overwrote the copies with stale ones and the gate went red; the change made it safer but
introduced the misleading text.
Size: 15 agent minutes (check whether the candidate's blob is in git log -- lib/<name> via git hash-object; skip or word the refusal; one test).
evidence: python3 -I -c "...relay_bench.lib_adoption_conflicts(cand, plugins/delegate)" after cp -RL of the plugin, then lib/relay_x.py changed
-> ['the candidate changed lib/relay_x.py (plugins/delegate/lib/relay_x.py links to it): port that edit to lib/ in a change of its own, then adopt again']
lib/relay_bench.py:94 new_candidate: shutil.copytree(src, dst, ...) (symlinks=False: real copies frozen at creation)
failing_case: relay improve new c --copy delegate (candidate holds real copies of lib/relay_toml.py etc. as of today); a lane then lands a change to
lib/relay_toml.py (25 commits in 5 days touched relay_queue.py alone); relay improve adopt c. Now: refused with "the candidate changed
lib/relay_toml.py (plugins/delegate/lib/relay_toml.py links to it): port that edit to lib/ in a change of its own, then adopt again". The
candidate changed nothing; the "edit" is master's newer code seen backwards, and porting the diff to lib/ undoes master's change.
Reproduced in a scratch tree: candidate X = 1, lib moved to X = 2 -> ['the candidate changed lib/relay_x.py ... port that edit to lib/ ...'].
Should: a candidate file equal to some committed version of lib/<name> (stale, not edited) is not called an edit: either it is skipped
(the link keeps master's current code) or the refusal says the candidate is out of date and names the next step (remake the candidate,
or diff against the version it was made from).
fix_hint: In lib_adoption_conflicts, treat a candidate file whose git blob hash (git hash-object) appears in `git log --format= --raw -- lib/<name>` history as stale, not edited: skip it (adopt_lib already leaves the link). Only a content never committed is named, and the message says "differs from lib/<name>" with the next step.
pass_cases: 1. Candidate made when lib/relay_x.py was "X = 1"; lib/relay_x.py committed as "X = 2" since; candidate untouched -> adopt is not refused with "the candidate changed"; lib/relay_x.py stays "X = 2" and the plugin's link stays a link.

2. Candidate whose lib/relay_x.py was edited by hand to "X = 99" (a content never committed in lib/) -> refused, naming lib/relay_x.py, nothing written (today's test_a_candidate_that_edited_a_shared_module_is_refused_by_name keeps passing).
3. Candidate equal to the current lib/relay_x.py -> adopted, lib/ unchanged, kit_* adopted (today's test keeps passing).
4. Any refusal names the next step a newcomer can follow without reverting lib/ (principle 10).
reason: tests/test_lib_links_adopt.py test_a_candidate_made_before_lib_moved_on_is_stale_not_edited passes at head, fails at bac1292e^.
findings.summary: adoption blames the candidate for a shared module that only master changed, and tells the agent to port that 'edit' to lib/ (which would revert master)

details: CONFIRMED by reading: test_lib_links_adopt.py imports relay_bench only; no test runs cmd_improve adopt with a candidate holding plugin copies
(git grep "improve\", \"adopt\"" / "cmd_improve" in tests). The wiring is correct today. LOW: correct but unguarded.
Size: 15 agent minutes (a temp ROOT via RELAY_ROOT is needed; may be costlier if cmd_improve's sync step needs stubbing).
evidence: tests/test_lib_links_adopt.py: TestAdoptLib calls relay_bench.lib_adoption_conflicts / adopt_lib only.
failing_case: Delete bin/relay lines 251-258 (the refused loop and its return 1). Now: tests/test_lib_links_adopt.py still passes (it calls
lib_adoption_conflicts and adopt_lib directly); adopt of an edited candidate then writes the history copy and active.toml and drops the
candidate's edit silently. Should: a test of the command (design pass case 7: "adoption refuses, names that file, and lib/ and plugins/ are
unchanged") fails.
fix_hint: One test that runs bin/relay improve adopt in a temp RELAY_ROOT with an edited candidate and asserts exit 1 and nothing written.
pass_cases: 1. relay improve adopt <cand> where the candidate's plugins/delegate/lib/relay_labels.py differs from lib/relay_labels.py -> exit 1, stderr names lib/relay_labels.py; profiles/active.toml, profiles/history/, lib/ and plugins/ unchanged.
2. Same with an equal candidate -> exit 0, lib/ unchanged, plugin lib links still links, kit_* adopted.
reason: tests/test_lib_links_adopt.py TestAdoptCommand test_adopt_of_an_edited_candidate_exits_1_and_writes_nothing passes; failing-without-refusal not run by me.
findings.summary: the refusal in relay improve adopt is not tested at the command; removing the bin/relay block leaves every test green

details: CONFIRMED by reading _link_problem: every non-link that is not kit_*/agent-roles.tsv and not a lib name falls to the stray message. The
allow-list is the design's; only the next-step text is one-sided (principle 10). Size: 5 agent minutes.
failing_case: A change adds plugins/relay/lib/guard_rules.toml (a plugin-only data file, not kit_* nor agent-roles.tsv). Now: precheck and gate print
"FAIL plugins/relay/lib/guard_rules.toml is a stray file under plugins/*/lib: git rm it (a merge leaves <name>~HEAD files)"; an agent
following it deletes its own new file. Should: name both readings: a merge leftover (git rm it) or a new plugin-only file (name it kit_* or
add it to the allow-list in relay_precheck._link_problem).
fix_hint: Extend the stray message: "... git rm it if a merge left it; a new plugin-only file is named kit_* (or added to the allow-list in relay_precheck._link_problem)".
pass_cases: 1. plugins/relay/lib/guard_rules.toml committed -> FAIL line names the file and the allow-list (or the kit_ prefix) as the way to keep it.
2. plugins/front/lib/relay_q.py~HEAD committed -> FAIL names the file and git rm (test_a_stray_head_file_left_by_a_distinct_types_merge_is_named keeps passing).
reason: tests/test_lib_links_adopt.py test_a_new_plugin_only_file_is_told_how_to_be_kept passes at head, fails at bac1292e^.
findings.summary: a new legitimate plugin-only file under plugins/*/lib is told to be git rm'd
